assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned a superconducting qubit into a controllable two-level system strongly coupled to a single microwave photon, giving dispersive readout, strong-coupling physics, and the architecture used by essentially every superconducting processor. It opened a new regime of light-matter interaction on a chip and is the natural continuation of the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits. The discovery itself is clean and reproduced widely.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 theory proposal, and Wallraff et al. (Nature 2004) gave the first strong-coupling experiment at Yale; the supplied trio covers theory and the two experimental lines reasonably. Others (Girvin, Devoret, Majer, Schuster) contributed decisively, so the three-name cut is a judgement call. I know this community closely and would flag that in committee.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across dozens of laboratories for two decades; the interpretation is stable and technology is built on it. Recognition is timely, with the 2025 prize already establishing the field's standing.
uncertainties: Credit among Yale, ETH and Sherbrooke theory/experiment contributors is not fully separable from the 2025 laureates' work and from Girvin and others.
My own proximity to the field (WACQT, Chalmers collaborations) means I should disclose a possible conflict of interest.
Whether the committee would view this as too close to the 2025 prize is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed trapped-ion quantum gates and later quantum simulation with controlled atoms, and the experiments (ion-trap gates, entanglement, digital quantum simulation) made quantum information processing a laboratory reality. It is a foundational platform for quantum computing and simulation, with the discovery being control of individual quantum systems for computation, and it is complementary to the 2012 prize on measuring single quantum systems.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the central theorists (1995 ion-trap proposal, cold-atom simulator proposals). Blatt is the leading experimentalist on ion-trap gates and simulation; Bloch is better credited on the optical-lattice side, which is covered in a separate candidate. Choosing Blatt over Bloch splits the compound candidate, and Wineland (already honoured) complicates the ion-trap story.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed in many groups over 25 years. Fault-tolerant computing is still ahead, but the physical discovery of coherent control is established, so timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: The candidate bundles ions and neutral atoms; allocation between Blatt and Bloch is unresolved.
Overlap with Wineland's 2012 recognition may make the committee reluctant.
Several other experimental leaders (e.g., Wineland's group, Monroe) are outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock (magic-wavelength trapping, Katori's proposal) combined with Ye's strontium clocks reaching 10^-18 fractional accuracy opened a new regime of precision measurement, with applications to relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. The idea is original and the experimental demonstration is clear and decisive.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first realised it; Ye drove the performance frontier and many-body clock physics. Two laureates are a clean allocation, though Hall and Hänsch (already prized) and Lemke/Ludlow, Takamoto and others contributed.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories confirm it and clock comparisons are routine; redefinition of the second is planned. Recognition is timely and low risk.
uncertainties: Prior frequency-comb prize (2005) overlaps; committee may view this as an incremental advance in the same field.
Contribution of ion-clock work (Wineland/Rosenband) relative to lattice clocks is a possible attribution dispute.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators (Kane-Mele), and its observation in HgTe quantum wells (Molenkamp, with Zhang's prediction), opened a major new regime of topological band physics. The importance and lasting impact are very high, though the 2016 prize covered topological phases earlier.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the central theorists; Molenkamp led the first experiment. Shoucheng Zhang's HgTe prediction (with Bernevig, Hughes) is a key missing contribution and he is deceased; Bernevig and Hughes are not in the credit list, and this complicates a fair three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups, including 3D topological insulators and ARPES. Maturity is high and interpretation is stable; timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) falls outside the supplied names.
Overlap with the 2016 Thouless/Haldane/Kosterlitz prize may count against it.
Interplay with B012 (quantum anomalous Hall) as a separate candidate is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Loss-DiVincenzo proposal for spin qubits in quantum dots, followed by single-spin control, readout and high-fidelity silicon devices, established a leading platform for scalable quantum computing. The discovery is both a theoretical concept and a sequence of demonstrations, and it is more technology-oriented than a single physics discovery.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo are the theorists; Vandersypen led key experiments (spin manipulation, silicon qubits). Petta and others (Kouwenhoven, Tarucha, Morello, Dzurak) are strong alternatives, so attribution on the experimental side is contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by multiple groups, and fidelities above 99% are reported in silicon, but scalability is not yet demonstrated. Recognition may be somewhat early relative to superconducting and ion platforms.
uncertainties: Which experimentalists deserve credit among Vandersypen, Petta, Kouwenhoven, Tarucha, Dzurak is unresolved.
Whether the discovery is the platform or the enabling technology is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle (Bistritzer-MacDonald) and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene (Jarillo-Herrero) created moire quantum matter, a whole new tunable platform. The originality and clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experiments. Dean, Young, Yankowitz, Kim and Efetov also contributed, and Santos/Lopes dos Santos earlier theory may deserve credit.
assessment.maturity: Discovery is from 2018; reproduced widely, but the mechanism of superconductivity and the correlated phases is still debated. Recognition may be premature by a few years though the pace is rapid.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is unsettled.
Prior theoretical credit (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell) is outside the supplied names.
Early for interpretation stability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and E91 founded quantum cryptography and made quantum information tangible, with strong ties to foundational quantum mechanics (Bell inequalities). Importance and originality are high, and experiments across many groups, including satellites, followed.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the central originators of BB84; Ekert's entanglement-based protocol is independent in concept. A three-person split is reasonable, although Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are decades old and widely realised; the physics is mature. Practical security is still debated, but the Nobel question is the concept, and recognition seems timely.
uncertainties: Wiesner (deceased) and others' precedence is a credit question.
Whether this counts as physics rather than computer science/information theory may be disputed.
Overlap with the 2022 Aspect/Clauser/Zeilinger prize on entanglement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened neutrino astronomy and a new window on cosmic accelerators, with clear measurement of a diffuse flux and the TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 associations. This is outside my own expertise and I defer substantially to colleagues in astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the conception and realisation of IceCube; Spiering and Karle were central in the collaboration and its predecessors (AMANDA, Baikal-linked). Credit is distributed over a large collaboration and early pioneers (e.g., Markov, Learned), so three names is a simplification.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux confirmed by independent analyses and the discovery is stable; source identification is still developing. Recognition is plausible now but source associations are partly provisional.
uncertainties: Which neutrino sources are firmly established is still evolving.
Credit distribution within a large collaboration and with pioneers is unresolved.
I have limited expertise here and am relying on general knowledge.
